title: Best Small Business Insurance 2026: 5 carriers for the 5-person consulting firm
description: Next, Hiscox, The Hartford, Progressive Commercial, Thimble — same 5-person consulting firm, real quotes for general liability + property + cyber + workers comp. Coverage gaps, BOP pricing, and which carriers fit each business stage.
lede: Five small business insurers. Same 5-person consulting firm. We pulled real quotes for a Business Owner's Policy (BOP) plus cyber + workers comp riders, and tracked where each carrier specializes.
methodology: Same fictional firm: 5 employees, $750k revenue, downtown office, occasional client-site travel. Quoted BOP ($1M/$2M general liability + $250k property), cyber ($1M), workers comp. Tracked premium, online application speed, claim service.

sections.heading: What a BOP includes
paragraphs: BOP = Business Owner's Policy = general liability + commercial property bundled. Standard for small biz. Cyber, workers comp, professional liability (E&O) are usually separate.
5-person consulting BOP ($1M GL + $250k property) typical pricing: Next $25-50/mo, Hiscox $35-65, The Hartford $40-70, Progressive Commercial $40-60, Thimble (on-demand) $10-30 per project.

sections.heading: Cyber + workers comp riders
paragraphs: Cyber liability ($1M coverage): Hiscox includes basic cyber in BOP. Next charges $15-25/mo add-on. The Hartford $20-30/mo. Progressive Commercial $25/mo. Thimble doesn't offer cyber.
Workers comp (5 employees, low-risk consulting): $300-500/yr per employee. The Hartford and Progressive specialize. Required in most states; Texas is the notable exception (optional).

sections.heading: When each carrier fits
paragraphs: Just starting / freelancer / under $100k revenue: Thimble (on-demand) for per-project coverage. Next for monthly BOP if you have a fixed location.
Established small biz / 3-10 employees / $250k-2M revenue: Hiscox or The Hartford. Both A+ rated; Hiscox is smaller-biz-focused, Hartford has broader industry coverage.
Auto-heavy / trades / contractors / fleet: Progressive Commercial. They dominate commercial auto + GL bundles.
Tech / SaaS / consulting / professional services: Hiscox (cyber-strong) or Next (digital-native).

faqs.a: BOP is cheaper than buying GL + property separately. Most small biz under $5M revenue should start with BOP. Beyond that, you'll outgrow BOP limits and need separate excess policies.
Yes if you give advice or provide services. Consultants, accountants, IT services, designers all need E&O — usually NOT in BOP, must buy separately.

next-insurance-bop.review: Next Insurance is the right pick for digital-native small businesses. 10-minute online application, $25-50/mo typical BOP, instant proof of insurance. Backed by Munich Re. Limited to standard small biz (no high-risk industries).
cons: Cyber is an add-on, not included

hiscox-small-business.review: Hiscox is the right pick for small biz under 50 employees, especially tech/SaaS/consulting. Cyber liability included in BOP. A+ A.M. Best rating. Broader industry support than Next.
cons: Less ideal for very large small biz

the-hartford-bop.review: The Hartford is the right pick for established small biz that values a 200+ year carrier. Strong dealer/contractor coverage, broad industry support. Bundled property + liability.

progressive-commercial.review: Progressive Commercial is the right pick for businesses with commercial vehicles or trades. Commercial auto + general liability bundles. Strong for fleet operators, contractors, electricians, plumbers.

thimble-on-demand.review: Thimble is the right pick for freelancers and gig workers who need short-term coverage. Hourly/daily/monthly purchase, $5-100/event. Buy and bind in minutes via app. Not for traditional small biz with fixed locations.
